attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, given as his own assertion, not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense statement about current industry practice. The normalised wording keeps the three named companies, the jailbreak-vulnerability qualifier and the robot integration.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: prototypes count and onboard compute is not required. Requiring jailbreak findings matched to each company's integrated model is demanding but fair, since Marcus named the companies. It is the choice to check each example that leaves the result open.

evidence.note: Google researchers used Gemini 1.5 Pro for robot navigation in July 2024. This shows earlier integration but not the configuration in use on 17 October.
Google's report says the Gemini 1.5 family is still vulnerable to jailbreaks. It does not match this to the version integrated into a robot or confirm the October state.
Figure's own disclosure of an onboard VLM and OpenAI-partnered models shows integration, but it names no model and gives no jailbreak findings.
A Tesla executive describes the October demo and human assistance but identifies no LLM. It neither shows nor rules out an LLM integration.
RoboPAIR jailbreaks robots from other companies (NVIDIA, Clearpath, Unitree). This does not establish vulnerability in Google, Tesla or Figure models.

reviews.rationale: Google's robot integration and its model family's jailbreak vulnerability are documented, but only before the target date and not matched to the October configuration. Figure's integration is shown without any jailbreak evidence. Nothing in the packet shows Tesla had an LLM in its robots. No item contradicts the claim. The packet does not settle the three named companies' state on 17 October 2024, so the claim is unresolved.
